We might have a more general statement for comma categories though
I'm not 100% sure, but I remember defining such an equivalence at some point, I just don't know if it ever ended up in mathlib

in particular, i believe the statement should be this:

import Mathlib

namespace CategoryTheory

variable {C D E F : Type*} [Category* C] [Category* D] [Category* E] [Category* F]
  (L : D ⥤ F) (R : E ⥤ F)

example : (C ⥤ Comma L R) ≌ (Comma ((Functor.whiskeringRight C _ _).obj L) ((Functor.whiskeringRight C _ _).obj R)) := sorry
where your case specializes to L = R = Functor.id F

Code

import Mathlib

namespace CategoryTheory

variable {C D E F : Type*} [Category* C] [Category* D] [Category* E] [Category* F]
  (L : D ⥤ F) (R : E ⥤ F)

variable (C) in
@[simps]
def commaEquivalenceFunctor : (C ⥤ Comma L R) ⥤ (Comma ((Functor.whiskeringRight C _ _).obj L) ((Functor.whiskeringRight C _ _).obj R)) where
  obj F := Comma.mk (F ⋙ Comma.fst _ _) (F ⋙ Comma.snd _ _)
    ((Functor.associator F _ L).hom ≫
      F.whiskerLeft (Comma.natTrans L R) ≫ (Functor.associator F _ R).inv)
  map {F G} α := CommaMorphism.mk (Functor.whiskerRight α _) (Functor.whiskerRight α _)

@[simps]
def Comma.lift (A : C ⥤ D) (B : C ⥤ E) (h : A ⋙ L ⟶ B ⋙ R) : C ⥤ Comma L R where
  obj X := Comma.mk (A.obj X) (B.obj X) (h.app X)
  map {X Y} f := CommaMorphism.mk (A.map f) (B.map f) (h.naturality f)

def Comma.liftFstIso (A : C ⥤ D) (B : C ⥤ E) (h : A ⋙ L ⟶ B ⋙ R) :
    (Comma.lift L R A B h) ⋙ Comma.fst L R ≅ A :=
  NatIso.ofComponents (fun X => Iso.refl _)

def Comma.liftSndIso (A : C ⥤ D) (B : C ⥤ E) (h : A ⋙ L ⟶ B ⋙ R) :
    (Comma.lift L R A B h) ⋙ Comma.snd L R ≅ B :=
  NatIso.ofComponents (fun X => Iso.refl _)


@[simp]
lemma Comma.lift_whiskerLeft_nattrans (A : C ⥤ D) (B : C ⥤ E) (h : A ⋙ L ⟶ B ⋙ R) :
    (Comma.lift L R A B h).whiskerLeft (Comma.natTrans L R) = h := by
  ext X
  rfl



variable (C) in
@[simps]
def commaEquivalenceFunctorInv : (Comma ((Functor.whiskeringRight C _ _).obj L) ((Functor.whiskeringRight C _ _).obj R)) ⥤ (C ⥤ Comma L R) where
  obj X := Comma.lift L R X.left X.right X.hom
  map {X Y} f := {
    app Z := CommaMorphism.mk (f.left.app Z) (f.right.app Z) (by simpa using congr($(f.w).app Z)) }

def commaEquivalence : (C ⥤ Comma L R) ≌ (Comma ((Functor.whiskeringRight C _ _).obj L) ((Functor.whiskeringRight C _ _).obj R)) where
  functor := commaEquivalenceFunctor C L R
  inverse := commaEquivalenceFunctorInv C L R
  unitIso := NatIso.ofComponents (fun F =>
    NatIso.ofComponents (fun X => Comma.isoMk (eqToIso (by simp)) (eqToIso (by simp))))
  counitIso := NatIso.ofComponents (fun X =>
    Comma.isoMk (NatIso.ofComponents (fun F => eqToIso (by simp))) (NatIso.ofComponents (fun F => eqToIso (by simp))))
  functor_unitIso_comp F := by
    simp only [commaEquivalenceFunctorInv_obj, commaEquivalenceFunctor_obj_left,
      commaEquivalenceFunctor_obj_right, commaEquivalenceFunctor_obj_hom,
      Functor.whiskeringRight_obj_obj, Functor.id_obj, Functor.comp_obj, Comma.lift_obj_left,
      Comma.fst_obj, eqToIso_refl, Comma.lift_obj_right, Comma.snd_obj, NatIso.ofComponents_hom_app]
    ext X
    · simp
    · simp

def arrowEquivalence : (C ⥤ Arrow D) ≌ (Arrow (C ⥤ D)) := commaEquivalence (𝟭 D) (𝟭 D)

I guess a potential issue with using a general equivalence for commas like this is that this is blasting through many defeqs (Arrow is a def for Comma (𝟭 _) (𝟭 _), not an abbrev, and I suspect the code above is using that 𝟭 (C ⥤ D) is defeq to (Functor.whiskeringRight C _ _).obj (𝟭 D)), and for arrows it could also be done "by hand" directly

Regardless, the universal property of commas given by the equivalence would be nice to have.

Here’s a direct definition.
Annoyingly, this code ran a lot into the bug where trying to use cat_disch for the autoparams would send aesop_cat into an infinite loop. Something is fishy here, and all the intros; ext <;> simp should be discharged automatically in an ideal world.

arrow equivalence

import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Comma.Arrow

namespace CategoryTheory

variable {C D: Type*} [Category* C] [Category* D]

@[simps!]
def arrowEquivalence : (C ⥤ Arrow D) ≌ (Arrow (C ⥤ D)) where
  functor.obj F :=
     Arrow.mk (X := F ⋙ Arrow.leftFunc) (Y := F ⋙ Arrow.rightFunc)
      (Functor.whiskerLeft F Arrow.leftToRight)
  functor.map η :=
    Arrow.homMk (Functor.whiskerRight η _) (Functor.whiskerRight η _)
      (by ext x; simp [dsimp% (η.app x).w])
  inverse.obj A :=
    { obj c := Arrow.mk (X := A.left.obj c) (Y := A.right.obj c) (A.hom.app c)
      map f := Arrow.homMk (A.left.map f) (A.right.map f) }
  inverse.map S :=
    { app x := Arrow.homMk (S.left.app x) (S.right.app x)
        (by simp [dsimp% congr($(S.w).app x)])
      naturality {x y} f := by ext <;> simp }
  unitIso := NatIso.ofComponents (fun _ ↦
    NatIso.ofComponents (fun _ ↦ Arrow.isoMk (.refl _) (.refl _))
      (by intros; ext <;> simp))
      (by intros; ext <;> simp)
  counitIso :=
    NatIso.ofComponents (fun _ ↦
      Arrow.isoMk
        (NatIso.ofComponents (fun _ ↦ .refl _) (by intros; simp))
        (NatIso.ofComponents (fun _ ↦ .refl _) (by intros; simp))
        (by ext; simp)) (by intros; ext <;> simp)
  functor_unitIso_comp F := by ext <;> simp

i haven't looked at this since the last time, but i did notice that the Arrow API is very leaky to Comma... this is probably ripe for a refactor, at the very least adding type-correct .left, .right and .hom projections, but possibly also just making it its own structure and adding its own Quiver.Hom structure (rather than reusing CommaMorphism)?

Hopefully, it should be enough to have the following abbreviations (and a few additional lemmas, which would be dsimp% versions of existing lemmas):

variable (f g : Arrow C) (φ : f ⟶ g)
variable {f g} in
abbrev Arrow.hom : f.left ⟶ f.right := Comma.hom f
abbrev Arrow.Hom.left : f.left ⟶ g.left := φ.left
abbrev Arrow.Hom.right : f.right ⟶ g.right := φ.right

actually, maybe we want Arrow to just be an abbrev instead?

For definitions of structures involving Arrow, the currently generated lemmas produced by simps should be mostly ok with this abbrev design. Ideally, it would be great if simps was able to generate lemmas for these abbreviations instead of the generic Comma/CommaMorphism fields. In any case, it would be better to invest time trying to improve our meta code in order to deal with such situations (which are quite common), rather than implementing custom structures for each particular case. (Note that similar issues may also exist for StructuredArrow, Over...)

I have no particular opinion about making Arrow an abbrev or not. If this works, and bench! is happy, why not! (We may want to keep specialized simp lemmas for Arrow though, with @[simp high] so that the Comma API does not leak too much in downstream applications.

In any cas, I think that the dsimped versions of the left/right fields, etc, should be very useful if we want to remove some dependency with respect to set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false. This is independent of the question of making Arrow itself an abbrev.

unfortunately i don't think Arrow.Hom.left and Arrow.Hom.right will enable the right dot notation, since there is no Arrow.Hom, and inserting an abbrev Arrow.Hom := CommaMorphism into the deriving clause to enable dot notation seems tricky to me, i don't think i can make that work without explicitly writing down instances...
(also, the easiest way to figure out what lemmas to amend is to make them a different structure anyway...)
Dot-notation is an independent issue (I have no idea how to make it work...).
so my idea regarding that worked, that's (for now) not the biggest issue
I am very much against making new custom structures if the only reason is that otherwise the infoview would be ugly (locally opening Arrow or Arrow.Hom should to the trick).

my other observation is that this probably will not fix the backwards.isDefeq.respectTransparency issues: afaict, the cause for those is that when we have f : Arrow T, we can't write f.left without breaking defeq.

right, my fix is to write the following:

variable {T} in
/-- `Arrow.Hom f g` is the type of morphisms in `Arrow T`. It is an `abbrev` for
`CommaMorphism f g`. -/
protected abbrev Arrow.Hom (f g : Arrow T) := CommaMorphism f g

instance : Category (Arrow T) where
  Hom := Arrow.Hom
  __ := (inferInstanceAs (Category (Comma.{v,v,v} (𝟭 T) (𝟭 T))) : Category (Arrow T))

rather than deriving Category
this works, as far as i can tell
Your PR is very much welcomed :-)
This is similar to what @Andrew Yang did at https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/354fc4dcb658ade8f54674e4fc034d279fa2c1e6/Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Modules/Sheaf.lean#L44-L46

unfortunately, my main experience with your suggested abbrevs is that it is merely a short relief, rather than a proper solution. Unification quickly finds that given Arrow.homMk ?m ?= g, it can use CommaMorphism.hom g, causing simple "applications" of lemmas to become badly typed... On the other hand, lean does not want to unify X : T with Comma.left (?_ : Arrow T) at instance transparency, which also worsens the experience... I think it is too complex to maintain this hybrid approach.
At this point, i'd say that our best options are probably either: make Arrow an abbrev/notation with no new defs, or make it a different structure from Comma.
